fleetMemory.LESSON: A restated copy is where a counting rule silently changes. This lane's own close artifact carried a per-county district-miss table copied from P-326's legacy census bucket instead of its districtOnFile field -- the numbers looked plausible, differed for only ONE of the six counties, and summed to 8,484 beside a total of 9,510. It survived the close and was caught only when the dry-run handoff had to state the numbers a second time and the two artifacts disagreed. The check that finds this costs nothing: make every per-county column sum to the project-level number printed next to it, in the artifact, at write time.

Write the invocation into the artifact by reading the job's own flags, never from the shape a flag usually has. This lane filed `parcel-setback-cells --county <fips> --dry-run` in both the close and the predictions, and the job has no `--dry-run`: dry run is the DEFAULT, and P-229's assertKnownFlags REFUSES an unrecognized argument before any store opens, so the documented command could not have run. The contract was readable the whole time in one call -- the job exports its parser, so `parseParcelSetbackCellsFlags([...])` answers the question with no DSN and no store. Probe the CLI contract of any job you document, the same way you probe its device.
fleetMemory.DEAD-END: Do not read a job's scope limits off its cloudbuild YAML header comment. `cloudbuild.parcel-setback-cells.yaml` still says Hays (48209) is 'structurally excluded (P-145 gate) -- there is no flag that can reach it' while the source it ships beside hardcodes IN_SCOPE_COUNTIES to all six counties, Hays included, and records the P-200 admission of 2026-09-14; that YAML is also pinned at _CONTRACT_VERSION 1.30.0 with older engine/LDT SHAs. The comment and the code disagreed, and only the code decides.
fleetMemory.LESSON: When a lane changes a WRITER's terminal cell shapes, the instruments that census those cells stop being able to see them, and that is invisible unless a test says so. Pin the blind spot (a test asserting the census reports the new fingerprint as unclassified) rather than widening another lane's instrument: an instrument's exclusion set is part of its contract, and quietly teaching it new shapes is how two lanes end up disagreeing about what a class means.

A reason string that is BOTH published text and a machine-matched key needs its redundancy checked by reading it aloud. The first draft of the district-miss refusal read '...the setback table for Lago Vista has no row for it, so the district's setback line is not on file; no district row is on file for this parcel; verify the district line with the city' -- three ways of saying one thing to a reader who only wanted to know what to fetch. Restructured so the clause that carries the class is short, distinct, and true in both sub-cases (table on file but no row / no table at all), with the specifics in the sentence before it.

Per-county expectations built from a city-level table are UPPER BOUNDS the moment any city spans counties. Six cities over-counted by 7,013 parcels, and the only reason it did not become a false finding is that the artifact states the allocation rule next to the numbers.
fleetMemory.DEAD-END: Do not try to produce pre-change evidence by running the post-change test file against pre-change source: it fails to LOAD on the new exports (SyntaxError: does not provide an export named 'CLASS_UNZONED_CITY_WIDE_LINE'), which proves nothing about the defect. A separate probe importing only APIs common to both versions is the instrument that can print both directions.

`git stash push -- src test scripts` does NOT make a factory tree pre-change: package.json/package-lock.json sit outside those paths, so the stash aborts and the next command silently runs against the NEW code (this produced a wrong pre-change transcript for a few minutes, caught only because the artifact is supposed to print its corpus version). Stash the files by name and assert the version you expect in the output.

PowerShell's `>` and Out-File write UTF-16 with a BOM; JSON artifacts written that way are unreadable to node's JSON.parse and to the close gate. Use [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText(path, text, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false))).
